information.content: Alpha-2 agonist sedative/analgesic used mainly in combination protocols for restraint or anaesthesia support in selected exotic species.
Avoid in cardiovascular or significant systemic disease, geriatric patients, pregnancy, diabetes and patients needing sympathomimetics. Vomiting and marked cardiorespiratory effects can occur.
Benzodiazepine used for emergency seizure control, anxiolysis, muscle relaxation and as part of anaesthetic combinations.
Poor sedative alone in healthy animals and may cause excitement. Avoid rapid IV administration and avoid or reduce in hepatic disease or severe respiratory depression.
Short acting injectable anaesthetic induction agent. Dose requirement is lower with premedication and administration should be titrated to effect.
Rapid or large bolus administration can cause apnoea, cyanosis, bradycardia and severe hypotension. Use oxygen and airway support.
Respiratory stimulant used where respiratory depression is present and the airway is patent. It does not replace oxygenation, ventilation or correction of the underlying cause.
Overdose may cause hyperventilation, hypertension, tachycardia, muscle hyperactivity and seizures. Avoid use without a patent airway.
Opioid antagonist used for severe opioid overdose or unexpectedly prolonged opioid effect. Onset is rapid but duration is short.
Can abruptly remove analgesia and expose animals to severe pain. Use ventilation rather than indiscriminate reversal in painful post-operative patients where possible.
Antimuscarinic used as an antisialagogue or to manage clinically significant bradycardia. It is longer acting than atropine and does not cross the blood-brain barrier.
Routine anaesthetic premedication is not generally recommended. It can thicken airway secretions and should not be combined casually with alpha-2 agonists.

warnings.warning_text: Can cause marked bradycardia, vasoconstriction and reduced cardiac output.
Avoid in systemic disease, geriatric patients, pregnancy, diabetes and patients requiring sympathomimetics.
Inject IV slowly and do not mix or dilute with other agents. IM injection can be painful and absorption erratic.
Can cause paradoxical excitement, aggression or prolonged recovery, especially with rapid IV dosing or repeated dosing.
Rapid or large bolus dosing can cause apnoea, cyanosis, bradycardia and severe hypotension.
Lipid emulsion is contamination-prone. Follow broached-bottle storage and discard times.
Do not use unless a patent airway is present. It is not effective for hypoxaemia without oxygenation.
Overdose may cause hypertension, tachycardia, CNS excitation and seizures.
May abruptly remove opioid analgesia and expose the patient to acute pain.
Repeated doses or CRI may be needed when reversing longer acting opioids.
Can make oral and bronchial secretions thicker, which may be undesirable in respiratory disease.
Combining glycopyrronium and alpha-2 agonists is not recommended unless specifically justified and monitored.

contraindications.contraindication: Cardiovascular disease, systemic disease, geriatric patients, pregnancy, diabetes or patients requiring sympathomimetic amines.
contraindications.notes: Choose a different sedation strategy in unstable patients.

contraindications.contraindication: CNS depression, respiratory depression, severe muscle weakness or significant hepatic impairment.
contraindications.notes: May worsen encephalopathy or respiratory compromise.

contraindications.contraindication: No absolute contraindication listed, but avoid unprepared bolus use without airway and ventilation support.

contraindications.notes: Airway obstruction and hypoxaemia require airway/oxygen/ventilation support.

contraindications.contraindication: Indiscriminate full reversal when ventilation can be supported and pain is severe.
contraindications.notes: Consider titration or assisted ventilation to avoid severe pain.

contraindications.contraindication: Routine premedication without a clear indication.
contraindications.notes: Monitor heart rate and secretion changes.

adverse_effects.effect: Bradycardia, vasoconstriction, reduced cardiac output, vomiting, diuresis, hyperglycaemia and arousal with stimulation.
Sedation, muscle weakness, ataxia, paradoxical excitement, thrombophlebitis with some injectable formulations and prolonged recovery after repeated dosing.
Apnoea, cyanosis, bradycardia, severe hypotension and pain on IV injection.
Hyperventilation, hypertension, tachycardia, CNS excitation, seizures and thrombophlebitis/extravasation irritation.
Abrupt pain, agitation or return of opioid-responsive signs; re-narcotisation possible after short duration.
Transient tachycardia, thickened secretions and arrhythmias after overdose.

monitoring.monitoring_parameter: Heart rate, perfusion, respiratory pattern, temperature, glucose risk and sedation depth
monitoring.notes: Atipamezole reversal should be available where appropriate.

monitoring.monitoring_parameter: Seizure control, respiratory pattern, mentation, hepatic risk and recovery duration
Ventilation, oxygenation, heart rate, blood pressure and induction depth
Airway patency, oxygenation, ventilation, heart rate and CNS excitation
monitoring.notes: Provide oxygen and treat underlying cause.

monitoring.monitoring_parameter: Ventilation, pain score, sedation depth and re-narcotisation
monitoring.monitoring_frequency: During reversal and for at least the expected opioid duration
monitoring.notes: Repeat dosing or CRI may be needed.

monitoring.monitoring_parameter: Heart rate/rhythm, secretion thickness, mucous membranes and GI motility
monitoring.notes: Do not use automatically as routine premedication.

pearls.pearl: Alpha-2s are not tranquillity mist. They are cardiovascular drugs wearing a sedative cloak.
Diazepam is excellent for seizures, but as solo sedation in a bright exotic it may bring jazz hands instead of sleep.
Propofol likes manners: slow titration, oxygen ready, airway plan made.
Doxapram can poke the respiratory centre, but it cannot open a blocked airway or invent oxygen.
Naloxone wakes up opioids and pain together. Titrate with a conscience.
Useful for the right bradycardia, but it can turn secretions into glue. Watch the airway.

species_warnings.warning: Monitor cardiovascular status carefully; IV and IM/SC dose ranges differ.
Reported amphibian dose is high numerically and part of a combination protocol. Specialist use only.
Use precise dosing in small birds; sedation may be unreliable and respiratory depression is possible.
Induction and recovery depend on temperature, species and route. Red-eared sliders may need higher dose for intubation.
Fish use is specialist and route/system dependent. Correct water and oxygenation problems first.
Full opioid reversal may cause severe pain; use ventilation or titrated reversal where appropriate.
Often preferred over atropine in rabbits due to atropinesterase variability, but still monitor HR and GI effects.
May be ineffective in green iguanas.

interactions.mechanism: Alpha-2 cardiovascular effects can conflict with or potentiate adrenergic effects.
Alpha-2 antagonist reverses sedative and cardiovascular effects.
interactions.recommendation: Use deliberately and monitor for abrupt arousal or tachycardia.

interactions.mechanism: May reduce diazepam half-life through enzyme induction.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor seizure control and sedation response.
Avoid or monitor closely for seizures/excitation.
Avoid unless essential; monitor BP and rhythm.

interactions.mechanism: Doxapram may stimulate adrenaline release while myocardium is sensitised.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid within 10 minutes of sensitising anaesthetic agents.

interactions.mechanism: High doxapram doses after morphine sedation may precipitate convulsions.

interactions.recommendation: Titrate to ventilation rather than fully reversing analgesia unless emergency requires.

interactions.mechanism: May precipitate when mixed with alkaline drugs.
interactions.recommendation: Do not mix in the same syringe.

interactions.mechanism: Combination may create undesirable cardiovascular effects.
Premedication and sedatives reduce propofol dose requirement.
interactions.recommendation: Titrate to effect with dose reduction.
